object_and_numeric_registry_fixture.method: Focused Rust consumers compile the relevant registry methods from the before and after production source and link the same existing framework dependencies for the real object and value types. Each registry installs only the described facts. Individual stripped executables and GNU size of the relocatable caller objects are reported separately from the full application. opt-level=s, one CGU. 35 fresh launches per revision on one CPU with alternating order. Registration excludes process launch. Conversion timings cover 100,000 lookups with a black-boxed result. Allocation counters report cumulative requested bytes during registration, not RSS.

object_registry.operations: register_object and register_upcast for each named control, then register_object for FerroObject. Hot paths convert an existing boxed Ref<FerroObject> to Option<Ref<FerroObject>> via the registered or borrowed-property API.

numeric_registry.operations: Install all 12 primitive nullable facts and the complete 12 x 12 ordinary/nullable numeric conversion table. Timed conversion is f64(88.5) to i32.

differential.serialization: one success byte plus eight little-endian payload bits per attempted conversion, using IEEE bits for floating values

relocations.method: x86-64 ELF. Decode R_X86_64_RELATIVE explicit addends and RELR inline addends, asserting unique pointer slots. Only .rela.dyn and .relr.dyn are included. .rela.plt is independent. Slot section identifies storage. Symbol families describe the pointed-to function, not who owns a table. Exact starts only; cross-family aliases are mixed. .data.rel.ro contains many kinds of Rust and application tables and cannot be ascribed wholesale to property/vtable owners. Non-relative dynamic relocations are reported separately by ABI type number.
